text:
Aisha: Hi all! Im Aisha, new joiner. First-day environment question: Windows 11, WSL2 Ubuntu, developing inside a VSCode devcontainer. I followed the onboarding dotfiles but running into two things: 1) asdf-installed python packages (pip) end up in a weird user site dir that VSCodes interpreter picker doesn't like, and 2) SSH forwarding from Windows -> WSL -> container seems flaky so pushing fails with "Permission denied (publickey)". Any quick checks?

Riley (devex): welcome! :wave: For the asdf/python bit, make sure your asdf python has pipx and that your PATH has asdf shims earlier than system python. Quick check: `which python && python --version && which pip` inside container. Also confirm devcontainer sets the right shell profile (e.g., .profile vs .bashrc) so asdf init runs.

Aisha: thanks. Inside the container `which python` points to `/home/vscode/.asdf/shims/python` but pip list shows packages under `/home/vscode/.local/lib/python3.11/site-packages` and VSCode still suggests the system interpreter.

Tom (infra): common cause: devcontainer not sourcing login profile. If your shell is non-login, .profile won't run. Add this to Dockerfile or devcontainer postStartCommand:
```bash
# ensure asdf is initialized for non-login shells
echo '. $HOME/.asdf/asdf.sh' >> $HOME/.bashrc || true
echo '. $HOME/.asdf/completions/asdf.bash' >> $HOME/.bashrc || true
```
Also for pip/package locations, prefer using `python -m venv .venv` then `source .venv/bin/activate` so VSCode picks it up. We recommend repo-local venvs for reproducible dev.

Riley (devex): +1 on venv. Our onboarding dotfiles used direnv for some teams; if you use direnv, add a `.envrc` that activates `.venv` or sources `export PATH=$HOME/.asdf/shims:$PATH` — then `direnv allow` after you open the folder.

Aisha: makes sense. Now, SSH: outside the container (in WSL) `ssh -T git@github.com` works; inside the container `echo $SSH_AUTH_SOCK` is empty and `ssh -v git@github.com` shows agent not available. I mounted `~/.ssh` as read-only in devcontainer.json but not the agent socket.

Sam (onboarding): FYI we document a few approaches. For Windows -> WSL -> container you can either run an ssh-agent inside WSL and forward its socket, or proxy the Windows SSH agent into WSL. On recent Win builds there's a socket at `/run/host-services/ssh-auth.sock`. Try mounting that into the container and set `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` env. Example runArgs: `-v /run/host-services/ssh-auth.sock:/ssh-agent -e SSH_AUTH_SOCK=/ssh-agent`.

Tom (infra): If you use GCM (Git Credential Manager) on Windows, it handles HTTPS but not SSH. Also if you mounted `~/.ssh` read-only, ensure private key permissions are 600; read-only mount can sometimes reset perms inside container making ssh refuse the key file. Check `ls -l ~/.ssh` inside container. If permission trouble, prefer agent forwarding instead of direct key file mounts.

Riley (devex): alternative quick hack: add a repo-scoped deploy key to let you push while you finish agent setup. Create a key pair inside the container and add the public key as a deploy key in the repo's settings (read/write if you need pushes). Not ideal long term but low friction for initial PRs.

Aisha: tried mounting `/run/host-services/ssh-auth.sock` as suggested and set `SSH_AUTH_SOCK=/ssh-agent` in devcontainer env. After restart, `echo $SSH_AUTH_SOCK` shows `/ssh-agent` and `ssh -T git@github.com` returns `Hi username! You've authenticated`, pushes now work. Also fixed the venv flow by adding `.venv` and a `.envrc` that activates it via direnv.

Aisha: for my dotfiles notes (so others on Windows can follow):
```bash
# WSL side (run once)
sudo apt install npiperelay # or grab npiperelay.exe and place in PATH
# create a socket proxy (example)
/usr/bin/npiperelay.exe -ep -s \\\\\\.\\\\\\pipe\\openssh-ssh-agent > /run/host-services/ssh-auth.sock &
chmod 600 /run/host-services/ssh-auth.sock
# devcontainer.json additions (partial)
"runArgs": ["-v","/run/host-services/ssh-auth.sock:/ssh-agent"],
"containerEnv": {"SSH_AUTH_SOCK": "/ssh-agent"}
```

Riley (devex): awesome, thanks for documenting. Please open a tiny PR to `dotfiles/README.md` with those steps and mention `wsl --shutdown` after installing npiperelay if folks still see stale sockets.

dotfiles-bot: applied asdf plugins for Aisha (nodejs, python) and bootstrapped default versions :white_check_mark:

Aisha: will open PR this afternoon. Appreciate all the help!
